newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hardie to expand U.S. output - paper.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hardie to expand U.S. output - paper.

text.p: Building products group James Hardie Industries Ltd would expand its Texan and Californian fibre cement building product plants, The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper reported on Friday.

"The Herald has learned that Hardie will expand the capacity of its Cleborne plant in Texas from 230 million square feet (MSF) a year to 290 msf (21.4 million square metres to 27 million square metres) by early next year," the newspaper said.
"Its Fontana plant in California is expected to boost capacity by 144 msf to 180 msf by Christmas," the Herald said.
"These enhancements plus the expansion of its Florida plant will deliver Hardie about 800 msf of capacity in the United States by its financial year end next March," the newsaper said.

Earlier this month, James Hardie said US$130 million raised from the sale of its global irrigation business would be used to expand its fibre cement building products operations, but it did not specify how large or where the expansion would be.

James Hardie Chairman Alan McGregor said in a letter to shareholders last month after his address at the August 1 general meeting that the company saw a significant return on its U.S. investment in particular in the year to March 1998.
He had said the general meeting that the profit in the current year to March 1997 was unlikely to improve on the net profit before abnormals of A$58.5 million posted in the year to March 1996
James Hardie's shares closed up 15 cents at A$3.15 at a new year high on Thursday.
